selection_reasons.household_solver: Modified Howard was the fastest passing household option in the reported comparisons.
selection_reasons.invariant_distribution: Power iteration with sparse CSR was the fastest passing distribution option in the reported comparisons.
selection_reasons.asset_range: k_max=5 is the smallest tested range with zero top-node mass and contains the distribution's support.
selection_reasons.grid_family: Its mean Euler error is lower (0.001089 versus 0.001204), and its distribution-weighted mean error is substantially lower (0.000805 versus 0.001472). I accept its higher overall maximum error.
selection_reasons.final_N: N=5000 gives the lowest mean, maximum, and distribution-weighted Euler errors among the tested grids, with a runtime of about 4.36 seconds.

shared_baseline_matrix_setup.timing_note: Shared matrix setup, excluded from each distribution algorithm's solve time

timing_notes: Part a sums utility setup and solver time, including all resumed batches.
Parts b/c sum distribution setup, solve and normalization; common Q construction/conversion is recorded separately.
Part d records student choices and has no numerical runtime.
Parts e/f/g include utility setup, solver, Q construction/conversion and distribution.
Part h times loading g solutions, fitting, writing the scaling JSON and recomputing Euler arrays/statistics.
Times exclude verification, figure rendering/export, script startup, checkpoint writes and user waiting; h also excludes final-array and table exports.
First SciPy imports can appear in the first case of a process; no repeated-run timing stability is claimed.
